businessModel: Free; ads, start-page traffic, sponsored navigation and 360 ecosystem (360 Security suite)
updateCadence: Frequent builds (16.1.6116.64 on 2026-07-17, 16.2.1038.0 on 2026-09-15); kernel upgraded rarely
summary: 360 Secure Browser is Qihoo 360's Windows browser popular in China, with dual-engine (Chromium + legacy IE) compatibility and bundled AI tools, but its Chromium 132 kernel lags current Chrome by about 20 releases.
bestFor: Windows users in China needing banking/IE-only sites

pros.title: Dual-engine compatibility
pros.detail: Switches between Chromium and a legacy IE (Trident) mode for old Chinese banking and government sites.

pros.title: Built-in AI tools
pros.detail: Version 16 Microsoft Store listing advertises a full set of built-in AI tools.

pros.title: Microsoft Store listing
pros.detail: Available from the Microsoft Store as well as the vendor site.

pros.title: Enterprise Xinchuang edition
pros.detail: A localisation edition runs on domestic OSes (Chromium 95 base).

cons.title: Old Chromium kernel
cons.detail: Chromium 132 (a forum noted Edge was already on 140) means missing recent security fixes.

cons.title: Ad and bloat history
cons.detail: Revenue relies on ads and start-page traffic; heavy bundled features.

cons.title: Opaque telemetry
cons.detail: Little published documentation on data collection.

faq.q: Which Chromium does 360 Secure Browser use?
faq.a: Version 16 uses Chromium 132, per the official site and Microsoft Store listing. Third-party pages showing older kernels appear stale.

faq.q: Does it have an IE mode?
faq.a: It is a dual-engine browser; legacy Trident mode is retained for old sites (per Wikipedia-style descriptions).
None found; focus is Windows (plus enterprise Xinchuang builds).

switching.note: Imports from other browsers; 360 account cloud sync.

spec.patchLag: Chromium 132 vs ~154 stable: roughly 20 releases behind (inferred)

securityHardening: Old Chromium 132 sandbox, no site isolation updates
webCompat: Chromium plus IE mode for Chinese sites

featureNotes.chromeWebStore: Own extension center; Chrome compatibility limited from China
featureNotes.uboFull: MV2 ext could run via sideload (unverified)
